analysis:
Examined all supplied additions and metadata against the canonical index and selected definitions. New local hold control introduces availability-sensitive IPC and persistent state under TB-003/TB-007. AddonHoldControl.swift:35–40 binds commands to process identity, freshness and lease bounds. AddonIPC.swift:61–98 bounds JSON size, leases and identifiers; this is parsing, not authorization. AddonPeerPolicy.swift:55–88 uses same-EUID kernel audit tokens, running-code requirements, team/identifier checks and hardened runtime, with extra identities DEBUG-only. AddonHoldPaths.swift:54–64 validates the final runtime directory; :76–82 probes locks nonblockingly and treats most failures as held. AddonHoldStore.swift:31–60 validates record ownership/mode/schema and uses exclusive temporary creation plus atomic rename. AddonHoldTelemetry.swift:16–42 logs operational fields, not prompts, keys or hold IDs. No direct changes to encryption, cache scoping (T-041), billing or serving authorization are visible.
Integration must inspect the supplied handler/lifecycle changes: bind claimed addon to authenticated peer and enforce ownership for hold references; ensure hold drain cancels inference and releases model/cache resources (T-010/T-028), while attestation, expiry and connection invalidation remain responsive (T-053/T-057). AddonIPCServer.swift:199–210 times out waiting without cancelling its detached handler; whether late mutations or accumulating tasks occur depends on handler behavior not supplied here. Also reconcile forced release and the observation-only machine-lock contract with model admission. These are unresolved contracts, not additional established vulnerabilities. The new add-on trust/availability contract should be reflected in the threat model; full boundary definitions and callers were not supplied.

findings.detail: Connections enter the eight-slot connection set before peer authentication, which occurs only after a complete request line arrives (lines 155–158 and 186–189). An unsigned same-UID program can open eight sockets and send nothing, denying service to the legitimate signed add-on for the 300-second idle timeout; reconnecting repeats the denial. The signature policy therefore does not protect availability of hold, status, release, or renewal operations. Authenticate the kernel peer token before admitting a connection, and bound incomplete-request time independently of received-byte activity.
findings.title: Unauthenticated connections can exhaust all add-on IPC slots

findings.detail: read() opens the hold-record path in blocking mode before checking that it is a regular file. A same-UID process can replace addon-hold.json with a FIFO containing no writer; open() then blocks indefinitely, so the subsequent fstat validation never returns .invalid. O_NOFOLLOW does not prevent this. This exposes the persisted-hold reader to a local availability attack whenever restoration reads the record. Open with O_NONBLOCK, then validate the descriptor as a regular file before reading.
findings.title: Hold-record validation can block indefinitely on a FIFO
